TEN MORE GAMEPLAY-FIRST LEVEL DESIGNS

Irreverents — candidate regions, not locked canon \| 22 November 2026

# Creative constraints

These are levels in the gameplay sense of Kirby & the Amazing Mirror and LEGO Star Wars: readable 2D side-scrolling spaces with memorable traversal, enemies, powers, secrets, optional routes, occasional heists, and co-op opportunities. They live in a genuinely interconnected, revisitable world, not an isolated menu of scripted missions.

Do NOT write a special lore premise, moral allegory, witty NPC speech, or Hero's Journey gag for every room. The role-obsessed world is backdrop and a reactive mechanic. Most rooms should just be great platforming. Dialogue very sparse.

NPCs have NO AI. They use authored routes, fixed animations and event triggers. Good-guy distress can quickly reverse by ordinary role-conforming behavior, but violent rage takes full disengagement and an incident-free wait until general heat cools below violent level; attacking, even defensively, prevents cooldown. Scaled reinforcements in ALL contexts require somebody to complete an actual report or signal. Good guys may report only in modes 2/3; bad guys can signal from business as usual when recognizing a threat. Guards can chase heroes between levels and clash with bad-guy factions, making three-sided battles. The most reliable place to wait out pursuit is an area guards can't readily access; such places are RARE in the between-level overworld, potentially more discoverable in elaborate levels.

The shared co-op party contains different recruitable functional character types and powers, but no specific count or final class lineup is approved. Proposed examples below use strong movers, tiny infiltrators, flyers, ice/wind/cutting powers, etc. Timed puzzles and environmental objects permit creative solo solutions when mechanically plausible. Never hard-code a restriction solely for a missing second human.

The levels should share a SMALL reusable interaction vocabulary: levers, plates, crates/weights, timed lifts, simple wind/fan, ropes and pulleys, water level states, moving platforms, grab/throw, a few breakable panels, alarm fixtures, hiding and traversal gaps, basic patrol lines and scripted waves. Special props are authored in finite ways; no arbitrary physics or simulated consciousness is required.

# 01 — IRON QUARRY

Layout: mountain ridge entry -\> crossing above a steep track -\> watchtower -\> branching ore depot -\> track loop around a deep pit -\> lower excavation -\> breakable wall into dark cave. The path from the lower pit can loop back to the ore depot; an inaccessible upper ledge later links to a different mountain region.

Platforming: minecarts move on fixed rails; players jump on roofs, duck under rock chutes, cross lifts and time jumps past falling boulders. Carryable rocks, carts and ore bins serve as weights and thrown objects.

Co-op: teammate holds lift lever while another rides and opens a gate from above; alternative push loaded cart onto the pressure pad or use a timed latch. Grappler moves boulders; flyer climbs an upper tower; tiny infiltrator slips beneath the ore conveyor.

Stealth: bad-guy bandits run a depot outpost with a visible lookout bell. Players can approach from lower cave route, disable bell or intercept caller. Recognition -\> move along authored route to bell -\> short windup -\> completed signal -\> reinforcement wave. Waves can scale indefinitely as further calls succeed; no automatic spawning from discovery alone.

Combat: push cart down slope into enemies; suplex an opponent onto another; launch a boulder into a brittle partition, opening a shortcut while defending against a wave. A wrecking setpiece is one authored breakable wall, not global destruction.

Refuge and replay: unguarded lower shaft above a difficult jump can be a refuge when pursued royal guards come from the townward route; guards can encounter bandits and fight them. A special small tunnel is a revisit incentive.

Build economy: rail/cart, weight, bell, lifts, one breakable quarry wall, bandit sprites. No bespoke dialogue.

# 02 — SHIPBREAKER COVE

Layout: tidal beach -\> hull of ship lying sideways -\> slanted deck and mast -\> suspended gangway -\> huge beached flagship -\> captain cabin -\> lower hold -\> sea cave looping back to cliff trail. Multiple crossings between adjacent wrecks.

Platforming: ropes and cargo nets, bobbing float platforms, falling barrels, swinging chain, anchors and gangplanks. Water can have two authored high/low states rather than a full fluid simulator.

Co-op: turn capstan to raise a cargo crate while a teammate rides it; hold another lever to place a gangplank; solo could pin capstan with heavy barrel/weight or time its release. Flyer reaches topmast, tiny hero squeezes through porthole.

Stealth: pirates on decks and a high lookout with a horn; approach through underwater holes or lower hold to sabotage alarm. Let a pirate signal, and reinforcements board from the side using a simple authored boat arrival animation.

Combat: thrown enemies collide with netting and deck; anchor release opens a new traversal hole and can knock down pursuers. Make deck sections marked breakable, with finite animation states.

Secret: flooded compartment with collectible; later traversal power reaches sea cave connection to a remote coast.

Production: mostly wood/rope/platform tile kit; horn, rope lift, one water-state gate, standard pirate attack and reinforcement sprites.

# 03 — CITY CLOCKTOWER

Layout: public ground floor -\> massive gears room -\> counterweight shaft -\> pendulum chamber -\> bell room -\> clock face ledge -\> rooftops and secret upper walkway. A forgotten stairwell descends toward undercity.

Platforming: leap between fixed rotating gears, ride counterweight lift, pass pendulum arcs, navigate giant clock hands and precarious narrow roofs.

Co-op: operate two controls at offset positions to rotate clock hands to bridge a gap; one player holds brake while another crosses. Solo: latch/weight/timing, or later flyer on roof. A small character can explore gear maintenance tunnel.

Stealth and good-guy response: tower staff and civic guards move on short schedules. Distress arises if heroes violate expectations; a reporting character must reach a bell/guard and complete a call before external authority responds. Personal mode 3 cannot be short-circuited by buying something or saying sorry; the player must escape, cease disturbances and wait for heat to cool.

Pursuit: Royal guards can enter tower from the city and follow through reachable floors. A hard-to-reach upper ledge or hidden shaft can provide a meaningful refuge—if the player has a suitable route and stays out of sight. A level title/door alone never resets chase.

Secrets: back of clock face opens to sky routes and a rooftop passage, and small maintenance space links to sealed archive.

Production: gear/pendulum animations on fixed paths, two switch states, a few good-guy barks/poses, upper hiding tiles.

# 04 — MOONLIT CONSERVATORY

Layout: old glasshouse entrance -\> lower watering channels -\> giant flower beds -\> climbing vine galleries -\> overhead glass walk -\> abandoned root cellar -\> hidden fungal passage. Several loopbacks through adjacent domes.

Platforming: springy flowers, folding leaves, drooping branches, rolling seedpods and vines as ladders. Plant enemies can be simple moving hazards with one attack.

Co-op: player A opens timed irrigation gate while B carries seedpod to planter; platform grows from a marked plot, giving access to upper route. Solo can weight valve open or exploit timing. Cuttable vine curtains provide revisit access if cutter power is newly acquired.

Stealth / fights: few gardeners and little need for combat; players can slip quietly through. If they deliberately attack good-guy gardeners, local witness/report rules apply, but the level is not forced into a heist or a gag.

Secret: small root tunnel leads to Mushroom Hollows (level 07); overhead glass walkway leads toward city clocktower. A later flyer reaches a hidden seed archive.

Production: three spring/platform behaviors, vine collision, water valve and plant platform animation; no procedural growth.

# 05 — PRISM SPIRES

Layout: pale stone footbridge -\> low prism chamber -\> mirrored gallery -\> large vertical shaft -\> roof terraces -\> central beam chamber -\> upper exit overlooking mountains. A side staircase returns to the gallery to form a navigational loop.

Core fun: beams of colored light bounce along a finite set of authored horizontal/vertical/diagonal paths. Move/rotate discrete mirror stands between predefined orientations; a beam powers a lift, reveals a platform, opens colored shutters, or switches a trap. Effects are clear, not arbitrary ray tracing of everything.

Co-op: one player holds a lever rotating mirror A while another aligns B, allowing a third to climb a temporarily illuminated bridge; solo can wedge A with weight, use timed latch or take alternative high route with a flying character.

Enemies: small glass sentries and hovering crystal monsters with very readable attack patterns. No town residents and no need for a major alarm. A single miniboss could attack by periodically sweeping an authored beam pattern.

Combat: use mirrors to redirect marked enemy projectiles or knock sentries into bright beam hazard; only a few objects are throwable.

Secrets: a mirror turned the wrong way illuminates an otherwise invisible side doorway, and a reflective shaft links to a buried cavern. Later power (if appropriate) makes the high balcony accessible.

Build: shared lever, orientation states, static beam segments, power receiver, one platform prefab; good visual payoff per unit code.

# 06 — FROSTLINE EXPRESS

Layout: outdoor rail station -\> cargo wagon -\> passenger wagon -\> open roof -\> guarded valuables wagon -\> engine -\> rear coupling exit. Backtrackable interiors and roof lanes; the train can arrive/depart along authored station links.

Core fun: a train level with jumping between wagons, low tunnels, shifting roof obstacles, trapdoors, couplers and moving cargo. Cheat visually: model wagons as a few fixed connected 2D rooms with scrolling scenery and vibrating props rather than simulating arbitrary moving train geometry across the entire world.

Co-op: one player lowers connecting cargo ramp while another crosses; release coupling to expose a hidden maintenance compartment; solo can hold mechanism with crate or use timed lever. Flyer can take roof path; small character can enter ventilation slit above luggage racks.

Stealth: ordinary conductors are good guys and can spot wrongdoing, then must actually signal to summon guards. An enemy raiding crew might independently board and have hostile signalers. Do not make every car a cutscene.

Escalating fight: raiders can attack heroes and guards; if players arrive already under wanted pursuit, pursuing guards can enter at station/platform connections and meet raiders on the train. Mixed fights arise through faction rules. Reinforcements require completed calls, not automatic 'new car = new wave'.

Secrets: concealed safe in valuables wagon, track maintenance exit at next stop and a mountain tunnel opening accessed via roof hatch when train is stationary.

Build: scrolling parallax + 4–6 wagon backgrounds, timed obstacle states, few coupling animations, guard/raider reuse. No requirement for continuous real-world moving position if that explodes scope.

# 07 — MUSHROOM HOLLOWS

Layout: sheltered forest stump -\> sloping root chute -\> bounce-cap chamber -\> thick spore corridor -\> enormous underground mushroom hall -\> dripping cave pool -\> root exit to conservatory. Hidden high tunnels allow several route choices.

Core fun: surprisingly joyful platforming. Small mushrooms spring straight up; angled caps launch sideways; large puffballs burst and obscure short sections; ride a moving beetle or timed stepping stones. A storm of spores briefly changes visibility, creating an opportunity for stealth but not a magic stealth button.

Co-op: one player holds down a large mushroom cap to create a spring-launch for another; return by knocking movable stone onto cap and climbing alternate path. A cutter can remove one web barrier; flyer can reach upper hidden hollow.

Combat: lightweight cave insects and a few territorial fungal creatures. No formal outpost, no mandatory alarm; an impressive visual challenge is an arena with bouncing enemies and thrown opponents ricocheting across pads.

Secret: a tiny crawl tunnel connects to old roots behind the conservatory, with a hidden route to high woodland. Few places to stand still in bouncing areas; actual safe refuge lies behind one difficult side route.

Build: reusable spring components with different vectors, spore overlay, basic patrol/bump enemies, two secret doors. Low story cost.

# 08 — OLD THEATRE

Layout: quiet public foyer -\> auditorium -\> huge stage -\> fly loft above curtains -\> backstage mechanical maze -\> costume storage -\> balcony and roof. A narrow trapdoor passage loops into the lobby.

Core fun: curtains hide sightlines, rope pulleys raise/lower large scenic flats, mechanical trapdoors and moving backdrops change access. Visual comedy comes from a real performer or guard continuing an ordinary animation while the players interfere; no exposition.

Co-op: one player holds fly-loft pulley to lift a scenery panel while another crosses; a strong character carries counterweights; tiny infiltrator can slip through under-stage openings. Solo can pin the pulley or latch an alternate backstage route.

Stealth: performers and stage guards are good guys. A thief can reach a locked props collection without being spotted; discovery of a knockout makes witnesses distressed, but a completed reporting signal is still required to summon outside guards.

Pursuit: if active royal pursuit enters from street, the curtains, dark catwalks and inaccessible fly-loft can become hard-won refuge. Once mode 3/wanted pressure has begun, pretending to be an actor does not instantly cancel it; must disengage and wait cleanly.

Secrets: an old trapdoor descends into sewer connection, roof links to clocktower district.

Build: two heights of curtains, pulley/platform geometry, line-of-sight blockers, scripted performers, alert contact, three-mode behavior.

# 09 — BONE CAUSEWAY

Layout: ruined road -\> narrow bridge above a chasm -\> fortified skeletal watchpost -\> branching bridge supports -\> high broken arch -\> ruined gate -\> underbridge tunnel into crypts. Thin alternatives span different heights.

Core fun: high-impact fights on narrow precarious platforms, wind gusts, destructible bridge braces, swinging spiked weights and skeleton squads. This level rewards grab/throw, careful jumps and route knowledge.

Co-op: one hero operates winch to lift bridge while teammate crosses and unlocks opposite mechanism. Solo workaround may use weight or freeze an activation lock. Flyer may avoid the lower risky bridge; tiny infiltrator reaches supports.

Villain signaling: skeleton watchposts have necromancer horn/altar. Hostile caller recognizes player as a threat in business-as-usual and rushes to signal. Successful calls summon increasingly dangerous waves from crypt gates. Interrupt or smash signaler and clear defenders, or flee.

Three-sided fight: if the player leads a pursuing royal guard squad into the causeway, guards and skeletons will fight by faction hostility. The player may exploit confusion to reach an elevated secret, but attacking either side prevents the good-guy wanted heat cooldown. A defensive brawl can become legendary.

Secret: underbridge vault with a rare power and a narrow concealed exit towards another land; very high arch may become a refuge if it cannot be reached by local pursuers.

Build: standard bridges/lever/winch, wind zones, cheap skeleton swarm animations and alarm/arrival prefab.

# 10 — THE DORMANT COLOSSUS

Layout: giant fallen stone-and-metal figure embedded in hillside. Enter by broken foot -\> climb leg shaft -\> knee chamber -\> torso gears -\> shoulder gallery -\> arm outside -\> head observatory -\> mountain roof exit. Multiple opened shortcuts let players return to lower areas.

Core fun: dramatic scale from ordinary 2D room composition. Platforms are giant fingers, armor plates, ladder rungs and mechanical gears. The figure doesn't need to become a fully animated physics character.

Co-op: one hero stands on plate to unfold a forearm bridge while another crosses to operate a latch; solo player can use a weight or later a special movement ability. Strong hero drags gear piece to restore a lift; flyer reaches head balcony directly.

Challenges: retracting machinery, falling gears, harmless wind tunnels, environmental projectiles and a handful of dormant constructs with simple fixed attacks. There's no shopkeeper, no villain sermon, possibly no boss at all.

Discovery: one control moves the giant arm into an alternate authored position, unexpectedly forming an outdoor bridge to previously inaccessible cliffs. Another opens the eye slit, revealing a high route toward prism spires. A chest in a finger compartment is visible early and attainable much later with a tiny infiltrator.

Pursuit: entering a giant's ankle is not automatically safety. Royal pursuers can enter accessible halls from the hillside, but a narrow shoulder vent or high hand chamber might be unreachable and offer a rare wait-out refuge. Entering the region doesn't clear an existing wanted level.

Build: big parallax sprite, standard platform collision, authored arm bridge state, lifts, hazards, few construct enemies. Highly distinctive visually for modest new mechanics.

# How the 10 regions connect

A compact non-linear possibility, NOT a fixed map:

City streets ↔ Clocktower ↔ Old Theatre; Clocktower roof ↔ Conservatory overhead walk; Conservatory roots ↔ Mushroom Hollows; lower woodland ↔ Iron Quarry; Quarry lower mine ↔ Prism Spires cavern; Quarry ridge ↔ Colossus mountain approach; mountain trail ↔ Frostline Express station; railway reaches high coastal stop ↔ Shipbreaker Cove; remote mountain/crypt passage ↔ Bone Causeway; upper Colossus ↔ Prism Spires and a mountain region.

Some links are obvious doors/roads; others are secret crawls, vertical climbs, destructible weak panels or one-way short drops that can become two-way shortcuts later. Inter-level connectors remain playable and comparatively exposed, with few truly secure places to wait out guards. Developed levels have richer topology and sometimes inaccessible refuges that reward knowledge/ability.

# Core reusable component budget

The quarry, cove, clocktower, conservatory, spires, train, hollows, theatre, causeway and colossus can primarily reuse:

1. Carryable crate/rock/barrel with mass/pressure behavior.

2. Pressure plate or lever with latched/timed/held variant.

3. Moving lift, suspended platform or rope winch.

4. Standard grab/throw/knockback with collision/hazards.

5. Finite tagged breakable panel/special wall.

6. Authored alarm horn/bell + interrupter + wave controller.

7. Scripted observer patrol/reaction with 3 emotional modes; faction-based hostility, no AI.

8. Hidden entrance/crawlspace/high ledge + collectible and shortcut state.

9. Timed environmental obstacle/hazard prefab.

10. Simple in-level persistence flags for open door, moved bridge, found secret.

Special local flavors can be cheap (spring direction, discrete mirror receiver state, water high/low and scrolling train background). Avoid physics simulation beyond what is necessary to express intuitive actions.

# A short gameplay contrast test

QUIET RUN: party goes through Quarry, rides ore carts, knocks out two bandits before they can ring a bell, reaches hidden cave, exits into Prism Spires. Nothing summons reinforcements, and the player enjoys secrets and puzzles.

WILD RUN: same place, deliberately allows repeated bandit signal calls and fights large waves. Eventually royal guards arrive pursuing the party from an earlier attack on the town; they enter the Quarry, fight the bandits, and allow the heroes to slip through a cave. The party then stays hidden and causes no new incident until good-guy wanted heat declines.

PLATFORM RUN: same party simply explores Conservatory and Mushroom Hollows for half an hour without talking to anyone and discovers three new routes. This run should feel just as worthwhile.

# Scope status and editorial guidance

ALL ten areas, names, individual puzzle solutions and geographic links are new brainstorming proposals, NOT project-owner-confirmed lore/production scope. The confirmed constraints are gameplay-first, low dialogue, small reusable 2D systems, novel character abilities/temporary powers, shared co-op party with solo improvisation, NPCs without AI, signal-required reinforcement, 3-mode good-guy response, persistent wanted pursuit and rare between-level pursuit refuges.

When fleshing out more, prefer concrete physical geometry and satisfying movement tests over paragraphs about what NPCs believe. Ask “what does the player DO here?” before “what is this place's glorious purpose?”
